title: Shading Vocabulary Types Across API Boundaries
pattern: Using symbol renaming (shading) to allow multiple versions of a library in the same binary when those versions exchange vocabulary types.
why_bad: While shading works for static utility functions, it fails both conceptually and programmatically when types are exchanged across API boundaries, leading to compilation or runtime failures.
detection: Shading configuration rules applied to library packages whose types cross interface boundaries between distinct modules.
counterexample: Shading a self-contained JSON parsing library whose types never exit the wrapping service.
fix: Enforce the One-Version Rule across the repository, keeping only a single, unified version of shared dependencies.
source: *Software Engineering at Google (Winters et al.), Chapter 16, p. 341 [143, 989]*
